note: A complaint, a grudge. 我对他有意见 doesn't mean you have thoughts about someone, it means you're unhappy with them.
The local earth god. You pass small shrines to 土地公 in villages and leave offerings so he watches over the neighborhood.
Brothers, and also your closest friends. Calling a friend 好兄弟 says you'd show up for him the way family would.

gloss: I, me (humble term used by men in public speech)
note: I, me, from a man addressing a group. 兄弟我 sounds modest and rough-and-ready, like one of the guys.

gloss: publicly funded institution, enterprise or foundation
note: A state-funded institution like a school or hospital. A job at a 事业单位 makes you think of stability and a pension, and your parents are proud of it.
Your career as a life's work. 事业有成 means more than having a job, it means you've built something people respect.
A farmer, and a social class as much as a job. You know 农民 can be thrown as an insult for someone unsophisticated, and it stings because of the rural and urban divide.
A worker, once the honored class. If your parents had a factory job, 工人 carries the memory of a secure 铁饭碗 that many lost in the 1990s layoffs.
Had better, after weighing it up. 还是走吧 sounds like you've thought it over and settled on this.
Not at all, flatly. 我根本不知道 pushes back hard, and you can hear some annoyance at the suggestion.

gloss: good; correct; conforming to a standard
note: Correct, textbook. When you tell someone their 普通话 is 很标准, it's real praise, and they're pleased to hear it.
A struggle, and a word with history. You think of the 批斗 sessions of the Cultural Revolution, though you also joke about your 思想斗争 over dessert.
A principle. When you're told 原则上不行 you hear that a way around may still exist, if you ask the right person.
